text:
A: Hiya, can you hear me alright? I'm Craig, Warrington.
B: Yeah. Kacper. Swindon.
A: Kacper, nice one. I've heard a bit about you, actually. Gemma said you're the night shift man.
B: Yeah. Shift manager, distribution centre. Nights and weekends.
A: Fair play. How many on your team?
B: About forty.
A: Forty, that's a lot of people to keep happy at three in the morning. What's the trick?
B: Erm. Don't really keep them happy. Just get the shift out on time. If the numbers are good, the site manager's happy, so.
A: (laughs) Honest answer, that. I'm in sales, flooring, so my whole job is keeping people happy. Facilities managers mostly. I let them moan, they sign the order.
B: Makes sense. Do you get a car with it?
A: I do, yeah, company lease. I'm picking the next one right now, it's the main topic of conversation in our house.
B: What are you looking at?
A: Kerry wants something sensible, an estate, for the dog and Alfie's football stuff. I want heated seats and something that looks a bit tidy on a client's car park. You into cars?
B: Yeah. I've got a BMW 1 Series, leased. If you're doing high mileage, check the excess mileage charges. Some of the company leases are fine, but if it's personal contribution, the BIK on the bigger engines kills you. Electric's better for tax. I looked at all of it before I got mine.
A: See, that's useful, that. The tax on the diesels is a killer, you're right. I did three hundred miles this week alone.
B: Electric probably works out then. If you can charge at home.
A: I've got a drive, so I could. Kerry'll be made up if it saves money. Do you keep yours clean? You look like a man who keeps his car clean.
B: Valeted every couple of weeks.
A: Mine's got a sausage barm wrapper in the footwell and a hi-vis vest on the back seat, if I'm honest. Are you after the next step up at work, then?
B: Operations manager. Within three years. On days. I'm looking at other places too, Amazon, Iceland. Whoever pays more.
A: No loyalty, I like it. I've actually had a rival sniffing about, hinting at a better package. I'm sort of using it to get regional manager where I am, you know.
B: That's what I'd do. Get the offer in writing first, though.
A: In writing, yeah, good shout. You're good at this. Do you still play football at all? Everyone today's a Wednesday five-a-side man.
B: Used to. Stopped because of the rota. Gym now, four times a week.
A: I clocked the shaker. I've got a dodgy ankle, so I just sort of stand in the middle now.
B: You should do some balance work for that.
A: That's what Gemma said! Standing on one leg brushing my teeth.
B: Yeah. She told me about my hips. She doesn't stop.
A: (laughs) She's a free physio, to be fair, I'm not complaining.
